page: Microsoft Azure D64ls_v5 is a low-memory, compute-oriented server instance powered by an Intel Xeon 8370C processor operating at 2.8 GHz. Built on x86_64 architecture with Microsoft Hyper-V hypervisors, it provisions 64 dedicated vCPUs across 32 physical cores with hyperthreading enabled. The hardware configuration features 128 GB of RAM, corresponding to a 2.0 GB per vCPU allocation, and includes L3 cache capacity of 48 MB alongside support for AVX-512 vector instruction extensions. This instance provides no local disk storage, relying on attached external storage, and includes no GPU accelerators or complimentary public IPv4 addresses.

Benchmark evaluations demonstrate top-tier multi-threaded processing power and high uncached memory bandwidth. The instance achieves strong results in stress-ng multi-core testing, PassMark CPU benchmarks, software compilation in Clang, image processing, and ray tracing. Uncached memory reads reach 292.88 GB/sec and writes reach 135.25 GB/sec, placing it in the top 25% of benchmarked systems. Operational performance is equally robust, registering 61.81 million operations per second in Redis SET operations and 53.15 GB/sec in static web serving throughput. Single-core performance across Geekbench and stress-ng remains in the average range.

The 1:2 vCPU-to-RAM ratio offers cost efficiency for core-dense, parallel computing tasks where high memory capacity per core is unnecessary. Eliminating local storage reduces base resource overhead for workflows utilizing remote premium storage. The instance is well matched for parallel software builds, high-throughput static web serving, batch encryption, and database operations. Conversely, workloads requiring large RAM capacity per thread or large-model LLM inference show reduced relative capability, as evidenced by low token generation speeds on 70B parameter models.
description: Microsoft Azure D64ls_v5 is a compute-optimized virtual machine equipped with 64 vCPUs (32 physical Intel Xeon 8370C cores running at 2.8 GHz) and 128 GB of RAM, yielding a low-memory 1:2 vCPU-to-RAM ratio. Built on x86_64 architecture and running under Microsoft Hyper-V, it provides dedicated CPU allocation with AVX-512 instruction support. The instance lacks attached local SSD storage and integrated GPU acceleration. Performance testing highlights strong multi-core CPU results, including high PassMark CPU, software compilation, and uncached memory bandwidth scores, while single-core metrics remain average. Dedicated memory bandwidth reaches 292.88 GB/sec for large block reads. Highly cost-efficient for parallelized, CPU-heavy execution without large memory footprints, the instance excels at software compilation, static web serving, and database processing. However, it displays limited throughput during large LLM inference tasks.
